responseText: {"title":"Marks Against Dark","question":"Which marks let a face become visible against a dark ground?","introduction":"Fifteen works share one condition: a dark field that could swallow any form placed against it. Some faces push forward through thick outline; others dissolve into the ground they occupy. Moving through the gallery, you can watch the marks that hold a face together—line, color band, crossed circle, bare tooth—and the moments when those marks stop being enough.","closing":"Each work returns to the same problem: a dark ground and a set of marks trying to hold a face in place. Whether they succeed, or only partly do, is a question each image leaves open.","chapters":[{"title":"Outline Holds the Line","introduction":"Three works where a strong outer contour is the primary reason a face or figure stays readable against its dark surround.","stops":[{"slot":"W005","whyHere":"A thick pink outline traces the central figure against deep brown-black; without it, the dense interior marks would dissolve into the ground.","transitionFromPrevious":null},{"slot":"W097","whyHere":"A loose white outline performs the same anchoring work, but here it frays upward into splayed finger-like lines, testing how far outline can stretch before it stops containing.","transitionFromPrevious":"Both works use a single enclosing line against darkness, but where W005's pink contour is firm and closed, this white outline opens and unravels at the top."},{"slot":"W213","whyHere":"The figure's yellow-outlined body is solid and readable; the face, replaced by a flat black rectangle, shows what happens when outline encloses nothing but more darkness.","transitionFromPrevious":"The white outline in W097 frays but still suggests a face; here the outline is intact yet the face it encloses is a void, reversing the problem entirely."}]},{"title":"Color Bands Cut Across","introduction":"Four works where a horizontal bar or broad color zone slices through the face, becoming the mark that most insistently declares a head is present.","stops":[{"slot":"W016","whyHere":"A single yellow-gold band cuts edge to edge across the eye zone; in a field of red-on-red, it is the one mark that unambiguously locates the face.","transitionFromPrevious":"W213's outline defines a body but leaves the face dark; here a single horizontal stroke does the opposite, marking the face while the rest merges with its red ground."},{"slot":"W057","whyHere":"Yellow-gold sweeps across the upper background and a thick bar runs the bottom edge; the paired red cross-hatched circles read as eyes only because those bands frame the dark mass between them.","transitionFromPrevious":"In W016 one band crosses the face; here bands bracket the figure above and below, so the dark mass between them acquires a face-like reading by position alone."},{"slot":"W127","whyHere":"Two flat horizontal bands—yellow-green and yellow—slice through the skull mid-face, indifferent to the anatomy beneath, yet their crossing makes the skull's interior suddenly legible.","transitionFromPrevious":"W057's bands frame a dark mass from outside; here the bands cut directly through a skull form, intersecting its structure rather than surrounding it."},{"slot":"W266","whyHere":"Two blazing cream ovals emit a flat horizontal light streak; that streak functions as a band, the one element that organizes the layered circular marks into a recognizable head.","transitionFromPrevious":"W127's bands are opaque and slice through; here the band is light itself, radiating outward from the eye zone rather than imposed across it."}]},{"title":"Crossed Marks and Competing Eyes","introduction":"Four works where X-marks, mismatched eyes, or split-face divisions are the visible device that gives the face its character against the dark.","stops":[{"slot":"W052","whyHere":"Two red X marks over the eye sockets are the sharpest contrast against the gold skull; they simultaneously locate the eyes and cancel them.","transitionFromPrevious":"W266's cream ovals radiate light outward from the eye zone; here red X marks occupy the same zone and block it, swapping emission for erasure."},{"slot":"W084","whyHere":"One eye carries a red X-crossed circle, the other a blue iris and dark pupil; the asymmetry between sealed and open makes the face feel off-balance in a way symmetrical marks could not.","transitionFromPrevious":"W052's two X marks treat both eyes identically; W084 splits the treatment—one eye crossed, one open—so the face holds two different states at once."},{"slot":"W278","whyHere":"A dark vertical line divides the face: warm amber-red on one side, cool blue-grey on the other; the split is the primary mark that makes the face visible as a face.","transitionFromPrevious":"W084's asymmetry is between two eye treatments; here the whole face is divided by a single vertical line, extending the split from feature to entire surface."},{"slot":"W274","whyHere":"The dark-green mass would be nearly formless without the two small ringed circles near the upper center; those circles are the only marks that propose a face inside the dense crossing lines.","transitionFromPrevious":"W278's face is split but fully present; W274's face is barely proposed—two ringed circles in a dense field are the only evidence a head is there at all."}]},{"title":"Surfaces That Enclose","introduction":"Three works where the face is held inside a curved or helmeted form, and the question is how much of the face that enclosure actually reveals.","stops":[{"slot":"W080","whyHere":"The rounded helmet-visor form encloses two asymmetric eyes and a gridded mouth; the pale washes and bright highlight suggest a reflective surface that shows a face without fully exposing it.","transitionFromPrevious":"W274's face is barely legible inside dense marks; W080 offers a cleaner enclosure—a rounded form with a bright highlight—yet the face inside remains incomplete and asymmetric."},{"slot":"W132","whyHere":"A large face fills the frame but colored loops spill past the jaw into the black surround, so the enclosure the head should provide keeps leaking outward.","transitionFromPrevious":"W080's helmet holds its contents; here the face has no such shell, and its marks overflow into the surrounding dark, dissolving the boundary the helmet maintained."},{"slot":"W303","whyHere":"The yellow hood is the most solid enclosure in the gallery, yet the face inside it is the darkest void—red slashes and bared teeth are all that remain where a face should be.","transitionFromPrevious":"W132's face leaks outward into darkness; W303 reverses this: the enclosure is intact and opaque, but the darkness is now inside, behind the hood."}]},{"title":"When the Ground Wins","introduction":"Three works where the dark field or a loud surround overwhelms the face, leaving marks that suggest a head without fully delivering one.","stops":[{"slot":"W298","whyHere":"An amber ground and crossing blue bands offer no stable face at all; the black masses and scattered dots read as noise rather than features, the gallery's most dissolved image.","transitionFromPrevious":"W303's hood contains darkness within a legible figure; W298 abandons figure entirely—the amber field and black masses offer no face to locate."},{"slot":"W057","whyHere":"Already seen for its bands, W057 earns a second look here: the dark central mass is so dense that the face-like reading depends entirely on the surrounding color pressure, not on any feature within.","transitionFromPrevious":"W298 has no face; W057 has a possible face, but only because the bright border forces the dark center into a head-like role by contrast."},{"slot":"W278","whyHere":"Revisited here as a closing case: the split face and escaping colored lines show a face that is present but under pressure, its boundary actively dissolving into the olive-brown ground around it.","transitionFromPrevious":"W057's face is proposed by its surround; W278's face is named by its split line yet still losing ground to the dark field at its edges."}]}]}
